headline: Only the marketing site is tracked: the journey is visible up to the pricing page and goes dark at the signup click (calls 3, 4 and 9).
68.5% of new visitors leave without an engaged visit, and Direct visitors engage at 18% against 61% for the rest (call 5).
New users read the troubleshooting help page more than any other help page (22 users, against 6 for the next), a sign that setup goes wrong for some of them (call 8).

journey_map.note: At least, because pricing and demo users can't be added together; 7 new users opened the demo page. No step rate: a visitor can reach pricing without an engaged visit, so the two don't nest.

Signup happens on the app's subdomain (user's answer). No click to it shows up in call 9, because GA4 doesn't treat a link to a subdomain of the same site as outbound, and there is no signup page on the site.
Site-visitor return is in the Early return area: 0.0% in week 1.

fix_first: Stage 4, Hand-off. It is the first stage that isn't tracked, and every stage after it is dark too, so the first fix is to track it. Among tracked stages the biggest drop is first visit to engaged visit: 68.5% of new users leave without engaging (call 5).

weekly_new_users.source: call 5: first_visit users summed by first-session week
weekly_new_users.flagged_weeks: w01, w02, w12: 81, 56, 290 new users, each 3 or more times the median of the other weeks (12)

scorecard.why: The property sees only the marketing site (3 hosts, no app host), so nothing after the signup click is tracked: sign_up, tutorial_begin and tutorial_complete never fired. 12 key events are configured and none fired in the window. Weeks w01, w02, w12 brought 81, 56, 290 new users against a median of 12 for the other weeks, so tracking or traffic quality likely changed around them, and a localhost session reached the property.

No signup page on the site and no click to the signup domain in call 9; the 9 outbound clicks went to social profiles (5), listings in AI assistants' app directories (2) and an AI assistant's connector settings page (2). Evaluation pages are reported as information.
Neither sign_up nor any onboarding step event fired in the window.
No key event fired, so there is no activation event to measure, and feature adoption can't be read either; call 7 returned 0 rows and call 11 was not run.
Signup isn't tracked, so these are site visitors, not product users: 0 of 240 new visitors in cohorts w01-w11 came back in week 1, and 0 of 210 in week 4. Information only.

The stage to fix isn't tracked, so the deepest tracked step is used (first visit to engaged visit). Direct brings 69% of new users and engages at under half the rate of the other channels; the gap is real (43.0 points against a 8.7-point threshold). The other 5 channels and mobile (26 new users) are too few to compare.
The connected Klaviyo account has no flows, so no email goes out after signup; the flow report for the last 90 days is empty.

top_fixes.fix: Send the product's own events to GA4
top_fixes.what: Add the app's host to this property's web stream (or link its stream) and fire sign_up with a method parameter, tutorial_begin and tutorial_complete around setup, and login on return visits. Every later stage depends on this.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 4: 3 hosts, all on the marketing site or localhost; call 3: none of these events fired.
top_fixes.expected_impact: makes stages 5 to 7 visible, so their drops can be counted and ranked
top_fixes.effort: medium: event code in the product
top_fixes.who: do this in the product and GA4

top_fixes.fix: Record the click on the signup button
top_fixes.what: Fire a click event with the button's location on every signup link, or set up cross-domain measurement between the site and the app, so the hand-off from visitor to signup is counted.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 9: 9 outbound clicks, none to the signup domain.
top_fixes.expected_impact: makes stage 4 visible: the share of visitors who start signing up
top_fixes.who: do this in the site's tag setup

top_fixes.fix: Pick an activation event, track it, and clean up the key events
top_fixes.what: Use the user's candidate (first data source connected and first report run) until it can be tested against week-4 retention, and mark it as a key event once it fires. Of the 12 key events that never fired, keep sign_up (it is in the plan), remove the 4 with test names, and check whether the rest should fire on the site at all.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 1: 12 key events configured; call 3: 0 of them fired.
top_fixes.expected_impact: gives the report an activation rate, a time to value and a week-1 return for product users
top_fixes.effort: medium: one event in the product, then settings in GA4
top_fixes.who: do this in GA4; marking the key event can be done here once the event fires

top_fixes.fix: Separate the Direct visitors who never engage
top_fixes.loss_counted_as: Direct new users who never had an engaged visit, x 30 / 84 days
top_fixes.what: Check the Direct visits for automated traffic and add a filter for it and for localhost, so the journey's base counts people. Then recheck the engage rate.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 5: 370 Direct new users, 67 engaged (18%) vs 61% for the rest; 300 unengaged Direct users over 84 days is about 110 a month. Call 6: 510 first-visit users on desktop, against 26 on mobile and 1 on tablet. Call 4: a localhost host reached the property.
top_fixes.expected_impact: if the check finds automated traffic, takes up to about 110 unengaged Direct 'users' a month out of the base, so every rate after it is read on people

top_fixes.fix: Start a signup-triggered onboarding email flow
top_fixes.users_lost_per_month: can't be counted: signup isn't tracked, so it is ranked after the fix whose loss is counted
top_fixes.what: A welcome email with one link to the first task, then messages triggered by what the user did or didn't do: no return, no key action, key action done, still inactive after about a week.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 12: 0 flows in the connected Klaviyo account.
top_fixes.expected_impact: can't be counted until signup is tracked; it goes after every new user who signs up and doesn't return
top_fixes.effort: medium: a flow in Klaviyo, plus the signup and activation events sent to it
top_fixes.who: do this in Klaviyo; send the signup and activation events to Klaviyo so the triggers and conversions work
